children.value: reads the JSON or text exports that cloud and cluster tools already produce and reports what they say is deployed: end-of-life runtimes, images, engines, cluster versions, and operating systems. Each result carries the importer, the file, and the exact place in the file the claim rests on, as an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer.
Offing never calls a cloud or cluster API. You run the export command on a machine with credentials, then give the file to

kubectl get deploy,sts,ds,cronjob,job,pod -A -o json > workloads.json
offing inventory workloads.json

Every importer reads one export file and produces items. The output is deterministic: results sort by file and pointer. An affected item means a lifecycle rule applies to the version the export names;

The importer does not judge instance classes, storage, IOPS, parameter groups, patch levels within a supported minor version, certificate authorities, Multi-AZ or read-replica topology, backup retention, encryption, or licensing. It does not judge MariaDB, SQL Server, Oracle, Db2, Memcached, or Valkey. It does not verify that an export is complete or current. It does not read an AWS account, role, or region, and it cannot see an object that the export omits.
